items.title: GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes following aortic valve replacement: a nationwide observational study.
items.abstract: GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce major adverse cardiovascular events among patients with diabetes, overweight, and obesity. Whether these benefits extend to patients undergoing aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS) remains unknown. Thus, we investigated the association between GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment and cardiovascular outcomes after AVR. Nationwide population-based cohort study including consecutive patients with severe AS undergoing TAVI or SAVR in Western Denmark between January, 2016 and April, 2022. Patients were followed until death, emigration, crossover, or end of follow up on May 12, 2026. Propensity score-matching was performed to balance confounding. The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, or aortic valve reoperation. Secondary outcomes included all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, aortic valve reoperation, with analyses accounting for the competing risk of death. Among 5259 eligible patients undergoing AVR, 292 propensity score-matched patients were included in the final analyses. During a mean follow up of 4.8±2.4 years, GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite outcome compared with controls (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.50-0.96, p=0.029). GLP-1 receptor agonist treatment was also associated with lower risk of all-cause mortality (HR 0.66, 95%CI 0.46-0.95, p=0.025). In competing risk analyses accounting for death, lower risks were observed for heart failure hospitalization (HR 0.67, 95%CI 0.48-0.93, p=0.018), and aortic valve reoperation (HR 0.69, 95%CI 0.49-0.98, p=0.037). Treatment with GLP-1 receptor agonists was associated with lower risk of cardiovascular outcomes including mortality following AVR among patients with severe AS.

items.title: Ten years of concomitant aortic and mitral replacement: trends, outcomes and the role of patient-prosthesis mismatch.
items.abstract: Contemporary data comparing double mechanical prostheses (DMP) vs. double biological prostheses (DBP) for concomitant aortic and mitral valve replacement are scarce, and the cumulative hemodynamic burden of simultaneous prosthesis-patient mismatch (PPM) at both positions has never been systematically assessed. DMP recipients had lower in-hospital mortality (1.9% vs. 15.2%; P = 0.010) and superior 7-year survival (91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003), but significantly higher stroke rates (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023). Combined PPM occurred in 64.6% of DBP vs. 14.8% of DMP (P < 0.001). Concomitant double valve replacement confirmed its high-risk profile, with an overall in-hospital mortality of 10.5%. DMP demonstrated superior unadjusted survival (7-year: 91.3% vs. 67.7%; P = 0.003) but significantly higher stroke risk (32.2% vs. 5.0%; P = 0.023), without differences in major bleeding rates at follow-up (8.2% vs. 11.3%; P = 0.478), although baseline differences precluded definitive prosthesis-type recommendations after multivariable adjustment. Combined PPM is highly prevalent after DBP (64.6%) and emerged as a univariable mortality predictor (hazard ratio 1.97; P = 0.046); given the exploratory nature of the cPPM definition and its collinearity with prosthesis type, this should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and warrants validation in larger, ideally multicenter, cohorts.

items.title: Arrhythmias in patients with transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and the impact of contemporary disease-modifying therapies.
items.abstract: Transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis (ATTR-CM) is an increasingly recognized infiltrative cardiomyopathy characterized by extracellular deposition of misfolded transthyretin fibrils, leading to progressive myocardial stiffening, electrical remodeling, and conduction-system disease. These pathophysiological changes create a complex arrhythmic substrate, resulting in a high burden of atrial, bradyarrhythmia, and ventricular arrhythmias that significantly contribute to morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in disease recognition, the optimal management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM remains challenging, with limited evidence guiding antiarrhythmic strategies and device therapy. In particular, the prognostic significance of ventricular arrhythmias and the role of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) remain controversial. Recent disease-modifying therapies (DMTs), including transthyretin stabilizers (tafamidis, diflunisal) and gene-silencing agents (patisiran, vutrisiran), have transformed the therapeutic landscape and may modify disease progression and arrhythmic burden, although their direct antiarrhythmic impact is not yet fully defined. This narrative review provides a structured overview of the mechanisms, epidemiology, and clinical management of arrhythmias in ATTR-CM, with a focus on clinically relevant decision-making and the potential influence of contemporary DMTs. Finally, it highlights key unresolved questions and areas requiring further prospective research.

items.title: Beta-blocker therapy and aortic growth in nonsyndromic ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms: a serial CT analysis.
items.abstract: The role of beta blockers in slowing aneurysm progression in patients with nonsyndromic ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms (aTAA) remains uncertain. We investigated the association between beta blocker therapy and longitudinal ascending aortic growth measured by serial computed tomography (CT). This retrospective single-center cohort study included 390 adults with nonsyndromic aTAA who underwent at least two contrast-enhanced CT examinations separated by a minimum of 2 years. Patients were classified according to beta blocker therapy (311 users and 79 nonusers). The primary outcome was the annual ascending aortic growth rate. Secondary outcomes included changes in the ascending aortic size index (ASI) and ascending aortic height index (AHI). Univariate and multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors of annual aortic growth. Baseline ascending aortic diameter was comparable between beta blocker users and nonusers (45.1 ± 3.5 vs. 45.2 ± 3.6 mm, P = 0.73). During a mean CT follow-up of 73.2 ± 39.1 months, annual ascending aortic growth rates were similar between groups (0.40 ± 0.54 vs. 0.45 ± 0.65 mm/year, P = 0.49). Likewise, changes in ASI and AHI did not differ according to beta blocker therapy. In multivariable linear regression analysis, beta blocker use was not independently associated with annual ascending aortic growth (standardized β = -0.031, P = 0.548). Exploratory subgroup analyses demonstrated numerically lower annual growth rates among beta blocker users with baseline ascending aortic diameters ≥48 mm and bicuspid aortic valves; however, neither comparison reached statistical significance. In this long-term CT-based cohort of patients with nonsyndromic aTAA, beta blocker therapy was not independently associated with slower ascending aortic growth or changes in indexed aortic dimensions. Larger prospective studies are needed to further clarify the role of beta blockers in limiting aneurysm progression.

items.title: Polyvascular disease by systematic vascular screening and adverse outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction.
items.abstract: The prognostic significance of systematically screened extra-coronary vascular disease in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains incompletely understood. We investigated the prevalence and prognostic impact of polyvascular disease (PVD) identified using a routine vascular screening strategy in patients with AMI. This retrospective single-center observational study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention. Ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurement and carotid ultrasonography were routinely performed during index hospitalization. PVD was defined as the presence of peripheral artery disease (ABI ≤ 0.90) and/or carotid artery disease, defined as carotid plaque according to the Mannheim consensus (maximal wall thickness ≥ 1.5 mm) or ≥50% carotid stenosis. The primary endpoint was a composite of all-cause death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, and unplanned coronary revascularization after discharge. Among 233 eligible patients, PVD was identified in 73 patients (31.3%), including 55 (23.6%) with single-territory PVD and 18 (7.7%) with multiterritory PVD. During a median follow-up of 419 days, the primary endpoint occurred in 43 patients. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated a graded decrease in event-free survival according to increasing PVD burden (log-rank P = 0.014; P for trend = 0.007). In Cox proportional hazards analysis, the presence of PVD was significantly associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, and this association remained significant after adjustment for age, sex, diabetes mellitus, and renal dysfunction. PVD is common in patients with AMI and is associated with poor long-term clinical outcomes. Routine systematic assessment of extra-coronary vascular disease may improve cardiovascular risk stratification.

items.title: PIK3CA Mutations in Advanced or Recurrent Endometrial Cancer: An Exploratory Molecular Profiling From the Phase II MITO END-3 Study.
items.abstract: Immunotherapy with chemotherapy significantly improves progression-free survival in advanced endometrial cancer (EC), especially in microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) cases. Despite this, for recurrent EC in the postimmunotherapy setting, new treatment options are urgently needed. The PI3K pathway is frequently altered in gynecologic cancers, including EC, representing a potential treatment target. In a preplanned translational analysis of the MITO END-3, we retrospectively analyzed the genomic abnormalities of 107 patients with samples eligible for next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis (FoundationOne CDx) with a focus on PIK3CA mutational status. In our analysis, the four most frequently mutated genes were TP53 , PIK3CA , ARID1A , and PTEN. PIK3CA mutations were detected in 51.4% (55/107 patients) of tissue samples. A total of 68 different PIK3CA mutations were observed, of which 64 were considered pathogenic and four were classified as variants of unknown significance, with the co-occurrence of two different pathogenic mutations in 2 patients. The most frequent PIK3CA mutations were found in the kinase domain, most commonly H1047R (11/68) and H1047Y (3/68), and in the helical domain, including E545K (4/68) and E542K (3/68). Notably, 24 different PIK3CA mutations out of 68 reported in MITO END-3 are considered predictive of response to PI3K inhibition with alpelisib according to current literature in breast cancer. Interestingly, PIK3CA mutations were observed in all The Cancer Genome Atlas categories. In this post hoc analysis from the MITO END-3 trial, we confirmed the high frequency of PIK3CA mutations in EC, establishing this tumor as an ideal candidate for testing of PI3K inhibitors in clinical trials.

items.title: Targeted immune modulation through smart biomaterials and programmable biopharmaceuticals: A review.
items.abstract: Immune-mediated diseases remain a major global health challenge, while current immunotherapies are often limited by systemic toxicity, poor tissue selectivity, and insufficient control over immune responses. This review examines recent advances in targeted immune modulation through smart biomaterials, programmable biopharmaceuticals, and hybrid biomaterial-biologic systems. A structured literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed studies published between 2022 and 2026 from major biomedical databases. The reviewed evidence indicates that smart biomaterials can respond to disease-associated microenvironmental signals, such as pH changes, hypoxia, oxidative stress, and inflammatory enzymes, enabling localized and context-dependent therapeutic activity. Programmable biopharmaceuticals further enhance precision by directing immune-cell behavior and molecular signaling through engineered biological mechanisms. In addition, hybrid biomaterial-biologic platforms combine environmental responsiveness with the potency of biologic therapeutics, improving immune targeting and reducing unintended systemic effects. Collectively, these technologies support a transition from conventional systemic immunomodulation toward adaptive and site-specific immune control. Despite significant progress, important challenges remain, including biological complexity, manufacturing scalability, long-term safety assessment, and regulatory translation. Nevertheless, the convergence of biomaterials science, synthetic biology, and immunoengineering is creating new opportunities for precision immunotherapy. Targeted immune modulation through programmable and responsive therapeutic systems represents a promising framework for developing safer, more effective, and clinically durable next-generation immunomodulatory therapies.

items.title: Practical Review of Role and Usage of Corticosteroids in Modern Neuro-Oncology Care.
items.abstract: Corticosteroids are commonly used in the treatment of neuro-oncology patients. Unfortunately, the benefits of steroids must be balanced against the potential development of complications. This review provides guidance for the usage of steroids in the management of neuro-oncology patients. Steroids should only be used as a temporizing measure in brain tumor patients to minimize symptoms secondary to mass effect from the tumor. For instance, because of the long half-life of corticosteroids, dosing should be limited to daily or twice per day, with the second dose given no later than early afternoon. Owing to its effects on multiple organ systems including endocrine, dermatologic, immunologic, gastrointestinal, orthopedic, and neuropsychiatric, prolonged steroid use can increase patient morbidity. They can also directly alter the potency of cancer-directed therapy including immunotherapy and chemoradiation. Steroid-sparing options, including bevacizumab, have emerged as means to minimize toxicity. Finally, the effects of steroid on tumor response has been formally integrated into imaging response assessment. Corticosteroids are an integral and useful treatment of neuro-oncology patients. We recommend using the lowest effective dose, with its frequency limited to 1 to 2 times per day and to taper them off as soon as possible to minimize toxicity and morbidity. The use of corticosteroids in clinical practice warrants specific consideration in the setting of immunotherapy and with assessments of imaging response.

items.title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy.
items.abstract: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR-natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields. Here, by bridging these approaches, we turn CAR-NK cells into magnetic biohybrid microrobots (CAR-NK microrobots) that achieve controllable long-distance targeted navigation at therapeutic doses (∼10 6 cells) in both murine and nonhuman primate animal models in vivo. CAR-NK microrobots are developed through genetic engineering with CAR structures and loading with magnetic nanoparticles for field-based navigation. Different magnetic field inputs reconfigure their swarms between vortex and ribbon modes, allowing dense aggregation for targeted navigation and further broad dispersion for large-area coverage. Using programmable magnetic fields, in vivo CAR-NK microrobot-based therapy is demonstrated for metastatic leptomeningeal carcinomatosis in brain's cerebrospinal fluid space. After intrathecal injection, the microrobots are magnetically guided long distance through the spinal canal toward the brain in vortex mode and subsequently spread over the target site in ribbon mode, as visualized by real-time angiographic imaging in a nonhuman primate model, providing a proof-of-feasibility demonstration in a nonhuman primate anatomical setting.

items.title: Owned dog population profile, dog ownership and bite risk determinants: Key steps to rabies control in Antananarivo, Madagascar.
items.abstract: Rabies remains a significant public health threat in Madagascar, with dog-mediated transmission causing approximately 1,000 human deaths annually. In Antananarivo, the capital city, control efforts are hindered by limited up to date knowledge on the dog population. This study aims to provide updated estimates of the owned dog population characteristics, identify determinants of ownership, and assess dog bite incidence and risk factors to guide effective vaccination and prevention strategies. Between 2023 and 2025, a longitudinal door‑to‑door household survey was conducted across 21 fokontany (administrative units) in Antananarivo. Of 2,518 surveyed households, 30.5% reported dog ownership, with 1,273 dogs recorded, yielding an estimated dog‑to‑human ratio of 1:9. The owned dog population was predominantly male (63.6%), with a median age of three years. Survival analysis in the selected study site indicated a median lifespan of 4.4 years and an annual mortality hazard of 16%. Vaccination coverage was low: 64.2% of owned dogs had never been vaccinated, primarily due to owners' time constraints, lack of awareness about the need for dog rabies vaccination, and financial barriers. Ownership was positively associated with household location and size, household head's age, education and income. No significant difference in bite risk was observed between dog‑owning and non‑dog‑owning households, whereas households with children under 15 years experienced a significantly higher risk. Rabies elimination among the owned dog population in Antananarivo requires sustained, context‑adapted interventions that address high population turnover. Annual city‑wide dog vaccination campaigns combining door‑to‑door strategies with fixed‑point sites are suggested to increase the chances of reaching a larger share of the owned dog population. Public health efforts must also prioritize paediatric bite prevention and expand access to post‑exposure prophylaxis to contribute to the global goal of eliminating dog‑mediated human rabies by 2030.

items.title: [Extreme values of alpha-fetoprotein in a patient with autoimmune hepatitis].
items.abstract: We present the case of a 29-year-old woman with a 5-year history of liver function test abnormalities who consulted for polyarthritis, fever, and jaundice lasting one month. Initial studies showed predominantly direct hyperbilirubinemia and elevated transaminases, alkaline phosphatase and gamma-glutamyl transferase. Viral hepatitis was ruled out by negative serology and toxic hepatitis by absence of exposure to hepatotoxic drugs. The antibody panel showed elevated antinuclear antibodies and positive anti-Ro titers. She also presented elevated polyclonal immunoglobulin G levels. Given the chronicity of the condition, alpha-fetoprotein measurement was requested for hepatocellular carcinoma screening, which results showed a value of 5966 ng/ml (reference value less than 10 ng/ml). Since these values were suggestive of underlying neoplasia (whether it is hepatocellular carcinoma or a germ cell tumor), magnetic resonance imaging of the abdomen and pelvis with contrast and transvaginal ultrasound were performed, which did not show tumor images. Liver biopsy evidenced interface hepatitis, confirming the diagnosis of autoimmune hepatitis. Treatment with corticosteroids and azathioprine resulted in normalization of both the liver function tests and alpha-fetoprotein. We therefore assume that the alpha-fetoprotein elevation reflected inflammatory activity and not neoplastic disease. Based on this case and similar reports, we consider that autoimmune hepatitis should be considered among the possible causes of extreme alpha-fetoprotein elevation. Se presenta el caso de una mujer de 29 años con antecedentes de alteraciones en el hepatograma desde hacía 5 años, quien consultó por poliartritis, fiebre e ictericia de un mes de evolución. Los estudios iniciales evidenciaron hiperbilirrubinemia a predominio directo y elevación de transaminasas, fosfatasa alcalina y gamma-glutamil transferasa. Se descartó hepatitis viral por serologías negativas y hepatitis tóxica por ausencia de exposición a fármacos hepatotóxicos. El panel de anticuerpos mostró títulos elevados de anticuerpos antinucleares, y anti-Ro positivos. Presentó además niveles elevados de inmunoglobulina G de carácter policlonal. En virtud de la cronicidad del cuadro se solicitó dosaje de alfafetoproteína para rastreo de carcinoma hepatocelular cuyo valor fue de 5966 ng/ml (valor de referencia menor a 10 ng/ml). Dado que estos valores son sugestivos de neoplasia subyacente (ya sea de hepatocarcinoma o tumor de células germinales), se realizaron resonancia nuclear magnética de abdomen y pelvis con contraste y ecografía transvaginal que no mostraron imágenes tumorales. La biopsia hepática evidenció hepatitis de interfase, lo cual confirmó el diagnóstico de hepatitis autoinmune. El tratamiento con corticoides y azatioprina resultó en la normalización tanto del hepatograma como de la alfafetoproteína. Estimamos por lo tanto que la elevación de la alfafetoproteína reflejó actividad inflamatoria y no enfermedad neoplásica. En base a este caso y a reportes similares consideramos que la hepatitis autoinmune debe considerarse dentro de las causas posibles de elevación extrema de alfafetoproteína.

items.title: Gallbladder Involvement in Pediatric Hepatitis A: Findings From an Italian Outbreak Cohort.
items.abstract: Gallbladder involvement during acute hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is generally considered an uncommon extrahepatic manifestation, although recent reports suggest it may be underrecognized. We evaluated the prevalence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of gallbladder abnormalities in a multicenter cohort of children hospitalized with acute HAV infection during an Italian outbreak. We conducted a multicenter observational study, including consecutive children with laboratory-confirmed acute HAV infection admitted to 4 tertiary pediatric hospitals between January and May 2026. Clinical, laboratory and ultrasonographic findings were collected. All patients underwent abdominal ultrasonography during the acute phase of illness. Thirty-three children were included. Gallbladder abnormalities compatible with acute acalculous cholecystitis were identified in 18 patients (54.5%), including marked gallbladder wall thickening (>7 mm) in 8. Children with gallbladder involvement did not exhibit more severe clinical manifestations or greater biochemical impairment than those without ultrasonographic abnormalities. Serum bile acids were markedly elevated in most tested patients but were not associated with gallbladder abnormalities. All patients were managed conservatively, and none developed gallbladder perforation, empyema, gangrene or required surgical intervention. Complete clinical recovery with progressive normalization of laboratory and ultrasonographic findings was observed in all cases. Systematic ultrasonography identified gallbladder involvement in more than half of children hospitalized with acute HAV infection, suggesting that this manifestation may be substantially underrecognized rather than truly rare. Despite frequent ultrasonographic abnormalities, the clinical course was uniformly benign, supporting conservative management in the absence of complications.

items.title: Histopathologic spectrum of focal liver lesions diagnosed by ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy and predictors of hepatocellular carcinoma: A single-center experience from Sub-Saharan Africa.
items.abstract: Focal liver lesions (FLLs) encompass a wide spectrum of benign and malignant pathologies, and accurate diagnosis is essential for appropriate management. Although advances in imaging have improved lesion characterization, histopathologic assessment remains the diagnostic gold standard for indeterminate lesions. Data on the histopathologic spectrum and diagnostic utility of ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy (US-PLB) in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) are limited. This study aimed to characterize the histopathologic findings of US-PLB performed for FLLs at a tertiary referral center in SSA and to identify factors associated with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We conducted a retrospective observational study of adult patients (≥18 years) who underwent US-PLB for FLL between January 2021 and December 2024 at Adera Medical and Surgical Center. Patients with indeterminate pathology results, incomplete records, biopsies performed for diffuse liver disease, or lesions classified as LI-RADS 1, 2, or 5 were excluded. Demographic, clinical, laboratory, imaging, histopathologic, and outcome data were extracted from medical records. Descriptive statistics were used to summarize patient characteristics and histopathologic diagnoses. Logistic regression analysis was performed to identify factors associated with HCC. A total of 119 were included in the final analysis. The median age was 56 years (IQR 45-65), and 59.7% were male. The median focal liver lesion size was 8.20 cm (IQR: 5.1-11.0 cm), with 38.7% presenting as multifocal lesions. No major biopsy-related complications were reported. HCC was the most common histopathologic diagnosis, accounting for 42.9% of cases, followed by secondary metastatic tumors (15.9%) and regenerative nodules (15.9%). Other diagnoses included chronic hepatitis (8.4%), cholangiocarcinoma (5.9%), and hepatic abscess (3.4%). Hepatitis B virus (HBV) and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infections were present in 14.3% and 12.4% of patients, respectively. On multivariate analysis, HBV infection (AOR 7.85, 95% CI 1.45-42.60; p = 0.017), HCV infection (AOR 9.03, 95% CI 1.41-57.76; p = 0.020), Fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) score (AOR 1.45, 95% CI: 1.05-2.34: p < 0.01), and larger tumor size (AOR 1.27, 95% CI 1.11-1.46; p < 0.01) were significantly associated with HCC. Ultrasound-guided percutaneous liver biopsy demonstrated a favorable safety profile for the evaluation of FLL. HCC was the predominant histopathologic diagnosis, reflecting the substantial burden of primary liver cancer in this setting. Chronic viral hepatitis and larger tumor size were significantly associated with HCC. These findings support the continued role of US-PLB in the diagnostic evaluation of indeterminate focal liver lesions and underscores the importance of viral hepatitis prevention, surveillance, and early detection strategies in sub-Saharan Africa.

items.title: Profile of migrant people with non-medically supervised use of pregabalin: a scoping review.
items.abstract: Pregabalin is a gabapentinoid drug used to treat neuropathic pain, epilepsy and anxiety. Over recent years, prescriptions and non-medically supervised use of pregabalin have increased in several European countries, especially within the French-speaking regions. These increases have been reported in young migrants, particularly those from Maghreb. However, the available peer-reviewed literature is poor with respect to the main characteristics of migrant people with non-medically supervised use of pregabalin and their trajectory of use. This scoping review explored both indexed scientific databases and grey literature to better identify the profile of pregabalin users, including their geographical origin, context and motivations of use, sociodemographic and psychiatric features. A search of relevant articles was conducted in several scientific databases of peer-reviewed journals, complemented by grey literature retrieved from reference lists of peer-reviewed publications and interviews with professionals involved in migrant support and healthcare. Two main populations of migrants using non-medically supervised pregabalin were identified. The first and main group consists of people coming from Maghreb, primarily from Algeria. They are commonly young socially marginalized men, who use pregabalin to experience euphoria or to cope with psychological trauma. These individuals usually migrate for economic reasons, and they frequently seek to specifically migrate to French-speaking countries for linguistic or family reasons. Pregabalin initiation is generally reported in the country of origin, and continues post-migration, in the context of precarious living situations or enrollment in criminal networks that provide an easier access to the drug, in exchange for engaging in different illicit activities. The second identified population with non-medically supervised use of pregabalin comes from Eastern Europe, and consists of older male individuals, who usually report using pregabalin to enhance or replace opioid drugs. In this second group, migration is motivated by economic or political reasons, and/or for getting access to healthcare services for chronic viral infections, such as Human Immunodeficiency Virus or Hepatitis B or C virus. They do not specifically aim to migrate into a French-speaking country. The increase in non-medically supervised use of pregabalin observed among migrant people in many Western European countries seems to be mainly related to two distinct migrant populations, i.e., Maghreb, and Eastern European respectively. Between the two categories of migrant people, motivations for pregabalin use, as well as migration trajectories, seem to be different, suggesting that prevention, harm-reduction and treatment strategies should be tailored to each group.

items.title: Association between serum transaminase elevations and clinical course in patients with familial Mediterranean fever.
items.abstract: To evaluate the clinical features, disease course, genetics, and treatment responses of familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) patients with elevated serum transaminase levels. The charts of the FMF patients with at least one year of follow-up were retrospectively investigated for the presence of elevated serum transaminase levels. The genetic and clinical findings and disease course of identified patients were compared with a group of FMF patients with no transaminase elevations. A retrospective chart review included 780 registered patients diagnosed with FMF. Forty-two patients (5.3%) were excluded because of the insufficient follow-up duration, associated viral hepatitis, alcoholic hepatitis, and biopsy-proven liver amyloidosis. A total of 83 patients (11.2%) with elevated serum transaminase levels were identified, and their findings were compared with a control group of 655 patients with no transaminase elevation. FMF attacks began at a significantly older age (17.0±12.9 vs. 12.4±9.0 years, p=0.01), and the percentage of patients experiencing more frequent (≥ 3 attacks/month) attacks was higher (35.4% vs. 24.1%, p=0.01) in the elevated transaminase group. No significant differences were observed between the two groups regarding age at diagnosis, delay in diagnosis, presenting features of FMF, CRP levels at baseline and during attacks, frequency of amyloidosis, and the colchicine dose, as well as the frequency of patients requiring anti-IL-1 treatments. The frequency of MEFV gene exon 10 mutations and p.M694V homozygosity did not differ significantly between the groups. Hepatosteatosis was observed by abdominal ultrasonography in 46.7% of the patients with elevated liver enzymes. A follow-up study after 6 years revealed that transaminase levels remained elevated in 21 out of 49 patients (42.9%), and one patient developed liver cirrhosis. Elevated serum transaminase levels can be detected in approximately 11.2% of FMF patients, and this finding is not associated with colchicine use or manifestations of FMF. Ultrasonographic evidence of hepatosteatosis was observed in nearly half of the patients. Follow-up analysis showed that serum transaminase elevations may persist in 43% of the patients, which suggests further studies to determine whether this abnormality is a feature of FMF or not.

items.title: Metastasis Extraction From Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Clinical Notes Using Large Language Model-Based Classification: Retrospective Comparative Study.
items.abstract: Identification of metastasis status in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a critical part of understanding disease prognosis, treatment courses, trial eligibility, and population-level cancer surveillance. However, metastasis status is inconsistently recorded in structured cancer registry fields, since manual abstraction of clinical notes is often an error-prone process. This challenge highlights an opportunity for leveraging large language models (LLMs) to conduct high-scale metastasis extraction from real-world clinical documentation. We conducted a retrospective, multicohort comparative evaluation of 3 distinct LLMs for 2 independent classification tasks: overall metastasis presence at any site and brain/central nervous system (CNS) metastasis presence. We evaluated model performance on 2 independent NSCLC cohorts: one with registry labels and another with manual annotations. We further explored whether our methods could analyze clinical documentation and recover missing information in structured registry fields. Patient cohorts were derived from the Winship Cancer Institute. Cohort 1 (n=579 patients; 24,887 notes across 69 note types; 2023-2025) used registry-linked metastasis fields as the reference standard. Cohort 2 (n=22 patients; 644 radiology notes; 2010-2021) was drawn from 2 completed randomized trials and used dual-annotated labels (Cohen κ: 0.93 overall metastasis; 0.88 CNS metastasis) as the reference standard. We fine-tuned the GatorTron-base encoder model for each independent binary classification task. We evaluated MedGemma-27B-text and Llama 3.1-70B using zero-shot prompting. A separate cohort of 675 patients with missing registry labels was used for an exploratory missingness-recovery analysis, validated against annotations of a random subsample. Our best-performing model was used to conduct further site-specific metastasis classification, based on available registry data. More than half (675/1260, 54%) of initially identified cohort 1 patients had missing or unknown registry metastasis labels. MedGemma demonstrated the best performance in overall metastasis classification (cohort 1: F 1 -score=0.80; cohort 2 patient-level: F 1 -score=1.0; cohort 2 note-level: F 1 -score=0.93). For brain/CNS metastasis, Llama3 performed best in both cohorts (cohort 1: F 1 -score=0.79; cohort 2 patient-level: F 1 -score=0.93; cohort 2 note-level: F 1 -score=0.86). The fine-tuned GatorTron model showed strong performance for classification of overall metastasis in cohort 1 (F 1 -score=0.72). Error analysis indicated that several model errors reflected incomplete registry labels, ambiguous clinical language, or missing documentation. In the exploratory recovery analysis, model predictions agreed with manual annotations at an accuracy of 0.90 and F 1 -score of 0.89. Additional site-specific metastasis classification by MedGemma demonstrated high performance for liver metastasis (F 1 -score=0.82) and bone metastasis (F 1 -score=0.79). All models demonstrated relatively high performance. The zero-shot generative models were more robust to nuanced documentation and context-dependent brain/CNS metastasis extraction. The fine-tuned encoder model demonstrated strong classification performance but may have been limited by potential inaccuracies in the registry reference standards during model training. This study further demonstrated the potential of LLMs in recovering plausible structured labels from narrative text, complementing cancer registries for metastasis ascertainment.

items.title: A retrospective epidemiological study of screening-derived solid cancer incidence proxy rates in South Korea before and after COVID-19 using Korean National Health Insurance Service data.
items.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted cancer screening and diagnostic pathways globally. Aggregate screening-derived indicators require cautious interpretation because they do not represent confirmed cancer registry incidence but might reflect program participation, referral patterns, and denominator composition. To evaluate pre- and post-COVID-19 changes in selected solid cancer screening-derived incidence proxy rates in South Korea, and to estimate model-based proxy rates through 2028. This retrospective ecological longitudinal study analyzed publicly available aggregate annual cancer-screening statistics from the Korean National Health Insurance Service (NHIS) and Korean Statistical Information Service (KOSIS) for six solid cancer programs (stomach, liver, colorectal, breast, cervical, and lung cancer). Annual proxy rates per 100,000 screened or eligible persons were calculated. Pre-COVID (2010-2019) and post-COVID (2020-2024) means were compared using Welch t-tests with Mann-Whitney U sensitivity analyses. Ordinary least-squares (OLS) forecasts were generated for 2025-2028. Interrupted time-series analysis was not feasible owing to an insufficient post-COVID observation window. Post-COVID changes in proxy rates were heterogeneous across selected programs. Breast cancer proxy rates increased by 17.1% (Welch p = 0.002) and liver cancer proxy rates by 83.6% (Welch p = 0.002); the liver cancer increase reflects denominator restriction to a high-risk population rather than a true epidemiological surge. Stomach cancer decreased by 23.3% (Welch p = 0.001), cervical cancer by 56.9% (Welch p = 0.005), and colorectal cancer by 25.8% (Welch p = 0.007). Lung cancer data were available only from 2019 to 2024 (program inception) and were interpreted descriptively. Aggregate South Korean national screening data show pandemic-era temporal associations with heterogeneous changes in selected solid cancer program proxy rates. These findings support an indirect screening-disruption and ascertainment interpretation rather than causal proof of a direct COVID-19 effect on solid cancer incidence.

items.title: The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China, 1990-2023, and projections to 2030: results from GBD 2023.
items.abstract: Alcohol consumption contributes markedly to the global burden of disease, but macroeconomic assessments of alcohol-attributable diseases in China remain limited. Using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data, this study quantified the macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China: alcohol use disorders (AUD), alcoholic cardiomyopathy (ACM), cirrhosis and other chronic liver diseases due to alcohol use (ALD), and liver cancer due to alcohol use (LCA). Disability-adjusted life year (DALY) data for the four diseases from 1990 to 2023 were extracted from GBD 2023. The macroeconomic burden was estimated using the value of lost welfare (VLW) approach, which combined DALYs with age-adjusted value of a statistical life year (VSLY) estimates derived from willingness-to-pay methodology. Results are expressed in 2021 international dollars and as a percentage of GDP. Temporal trends were evaluated using Joinpoint regression analysis, and exploratory forecasts to 2030 were generated using ARIMA, XGBoost, and LightGBM models. From 1990 to 2023, VLW increased substantially for all four diseases: AUD from $1.84 billion to $32.40 billion; ACM, $0.04 to $0.53 billion; ALD, $0.22 to $3.26 billion; and LCA, $0.09 to $2.48 billion. Joinpoint regression confirmed continuously increasing trends (all AAPC > 0, all p  < 0.001). Males predominated across all conditions, with male-to-female VLW ratios of 7:1 (AUD), 10:1 (ALD), 3:1 (LCA), and 14:1 (ACM) in 2023. Age at peak VLW varied: 35-39 years for AUD, 50-59 years for ALD, 65-69 years for LCA, and 50-54 years for ACM (shifted from 35-39 years in 1990). Conditional on the continuation of their respective historical trends, the three models produced divergent exploratory projections to 2030. The macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases in China increased markedly from 1990 to 2023, with AUD consistently dominating and the burden overwhelmingly concentrated among males aged 35-64 years. This is the first study to quantify the macroeconomic burden of four alcohol-attributable diseases (AUD, ACM, ALD, and LCA) in China from 1990 to 2023 with projections to 2030.The economic burden of each disease increased considerably over the 34-year period. AUD consistently accounted for a far higher VLW than the other three diseases, whereas LCA showed the most pronounced increase.This study suggests primary prevention (health education, reduced availability) for young adults aged 20–35 years, and secondary prevention for males aged 35–64 years: workplace-based AUD screening for ages 35–49 years and integrated hepatology-cardiology surveillance for ages 50–64 years.

items.title: Fluorogenic RNA aptamers in cancer: emerging platforms for molecular imaging, biosensing, and precision oncology.
items.abstract: Fluorogenic RNA aptamers have emerged as powerful molecular tools for cancer imaging, biosensing, and biomarker detection due to their high specificity, low background fluorescence, and genetic encodability. These short RNA molecules activate fluorescence upon binding specific fluorogens, enabling real-time visualization of intracellular targets and dynamic molecular processes in living systems. Recent advances in RNA structural engineering, fluorophore optimization, and biosensor integration have significantly expanded the translational applications of fluorogenic aptamers in oncology. This mini-review summarizes the structural principles, fluorescence activation mechanisms, and cancer-related applications of fluorogenic RNA aptamers and related nucleic acid biosensors. Foundational studies describing the architecture of fluorogenic aptamer families, including Spinach, Broccoli, Mango, Pepper, Squash, and Beetroot, are discussed with emphasis on G-quadruplex-mediated fluorogen stabilization and fluorescence enhancement. Furthermore, recent developments in CRISPR/Cas-assisted fluorogenic biosensors, dual-color RNA imaging systems, fluorogenic DNAzymes, and amplification-driven aptamer platforms are highlighted. Direct applications across multiple malignancies, including brain, breast, colorectal, liver, lung, prostate, and skin cancers, demonstrate the growing utility of these technologies for tumor-associated RNA detection, epigenetic biomarker analysis, molecular imaging, and therapeutic monitoring. In addition, advances in fluorescence brightness, structural stability, and multiplex imaging strategies have improved the sensitivity and adaptability of fluorogenic RNA systems for complex biological environments. Despite current limitations related to RNA stability, intracellular delivery, and tissue penetration, fluorogenic RNA aptamers represent highly promising tools for next-generation precision oncology. Continued integration with nanotechnology, live-cell imaging, artificial intelligence, and molecular diagnostics is expected to enhance further their clinical and translational potential in cancer research and personalized medicine.
